cross_market_insights: The head term is transactional and local in every market: retail products (AU), hire companies and local packs (Melbourne, Brisbane, London), directories (London). No editorial guide ranks in the organic top 3 in any market checked.

Editorial guides appear only in the image pack and the Brisbane AI Overview (US and UK publishers' idea galleries and one 'ultimate guide'). That is the realistic entry point for an editorial page: images, AI Overview citation and the long tail ('wedding lighting ideas', 'outdoor wedding lighting', 'candle wedding decor').
AU volume is modest (140 a month head term; 90 for fairy lights; 50 candles; 40 outdoor). Commercial value is high (HIGH competition on 5 of 6 terms), which matches a supplier-heavy SERP.

No result in any market covers lighting a reception abroad: sunset times at the destination, generators and power at villas, beaches and vineyards, wind and humidity, open-flame rules, or who coordinates the lighting crew with the venue, photographer and band. This is the gap.
The Brisbane AI Overview leans on price and buying tips for DIY festoon and fairy lights. That is the bargain_hunter intent; we should not compete on DIY product advice.
No People Also Ask box was shown in any market, so FAQs should come from reader questions implied by related searches and the brief's must_include, not from PAA.
payload.recommended_angle: The luxury reception lighting plan for a wedding abroad: how the three layers (ambient, accent, task) are built at four venue types (villa terrace, beach or island, vineyard, ballroom), when to switch from sunset to candlelight, what reads well on camera, and the unseen work (power, generators, weather, open-flame rules, crew timing) that a Wedded Advisor coordinates with the venue and lighting supplier.
